mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in quarters where FEDFUNDS rises by > 0.5% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a flattening industrial production trend (INDPRO) signals weakening aggregate demand, which is expected to depress earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND INDPRO monthly change < 0 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% combined with a concurrent rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) above trend indicates a tight labor market that pressures firms to raise wages and prices, compressing profit margins and ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% AND PAYEMS > trend for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average, without a corresponding decline in unemployment (UNRATE), signals supply-side disruptions that raise input costs and reduce output, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE not falling
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports broader economic activity, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods when HOUST > 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) of at least 0.75 percentage points signals an emergency easing in response to a financial shock, which lowers borrowing costs and supports risk assets, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops by ≥ 0.75% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) following a ≥ 0.75% one-month FEDFUNDS decline.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two consecutive months indicates a statistical artifact from labor force re-entry after a downturn, which is typically followed by a normalization of labor market conditions and a positive S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) exceeding 5% while personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) grow below 2% signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a consumer-driven economic slowdown and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.
